transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-07
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Avery Chen, Priya Raman, Darius King, Lina Alvarez (Redwood) — Liam O'Connor, Maya Lopez, Raj Patel, Tessa Wu (NimbusCompute)

Summary (auto): Introductory partner discovery between Redwood Inference and NimbusCompute. Discussed potential reseller/integration models, technical compat for private/dedicated deployments, benchmark approach, security/compliance asks, and next steps to run a POC.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is Avery from Redwood, AE. Um, we've got Priya our solutions engineer on the line and Darius who runs partnerships; appreciate you all making time.
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: Yep thanks Avery, Liam here. We've been looking to expand our partner ecosystem for GPU-based inference offerings. Quick note, Tessa and Raj from our team are on as well.
[00:20] Priya Raman: Hi all; quick icebreaker — curious what your main objectives are for a partnership, is this reseller, co-sell, or more of a technical integration?
[00:28] Maya Lopez: Great question. For Nimbus, primary ask is reseller + marketplace listing so customers can pick Redwood-managed inference via our console. Secondary is co-managed private deployments for larger enterprise clients.
[00:39] Raj Patel: Also technical — we want to make sure our hardware and networking (NVLink pods, etc.) map cleanly to Redwood's dedicated capacity offering. We need to understand kernel support, driver matrix, and what profile you validate.
[00:51] Priya Raman: Makes sense. Redwood's Dedicated runs on a GPU-optimized runtime; we do kernel selection at model load time and maintain a catalog of validated hardware profiles. There's some nuance with NVLink vs. non-NVLink for multi-GPU models — performance differs and we typically recommend certain topologies.
[01:08] Liam O'Connor: On the commercial side, what's the typical revenue share or reseller margin you offer? Any minimum commitments?
[01:15] Avery Chen: We have flexible models — marketplace listing with referral credit, or reseller with discounts on committed capacity. For Dedicated we talk reserved capacity commitments; for marketplace listing it's lighter-touch. We'll send the partner one-pager and pricing bands after.
[01:27] Tessa Wu: On compliance — do you support customer-managed KMS and have audit logs accessible for our enterprise buyers?
[01:34] Darius King: Yes — for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM, and we expose audit logs and trace hooks. We also have SOC 2 Type II. We can share the security pack; some of the docs are gated but we'll get them to you.
[01:48] Maya Lopez: Awesome. Also, do you offer a private control plane deployment in our VPC or is it always customer on-prem? We have customers who are in-regulation and need VPC options.
[01:57] Priya Raman: We support VPC-hosted private control plane and on-prem package for air-gapped cases. The VPC option is common for partners integrating into their portal.
[02:05] Raj Patel: From a latency perspective, do you do prefix/KV caching? We care about 99p latency more than avg for interactive workloads.
[02:12] Priya Raman: Yes — runtime handles KV cache and prefix caching, and we have SLOs for p50/p95/p99 depending on the deployment profile. For Dedicated we can tune batching/caching aggressively. We'll share past benchmark numbers but we recommend running your own pilot since hardware topology affects numbers.
[02:27] Avery Chen: For the POC we typically ask partners to provide a small representative workload and we run a joint benchmark using our harness. Priya will share the spreadsheet with test configs.
[02:36] Liam O'Connor: Cool. A couple of technical questions: do you support mixed precision quantization? And what's the model onboarding process if a customer wants a custom model?
[02:44] Priya Raman: We support quantization-friendly execution paths and recommend certain quant profiles by model family. For custom models we have a model onboarding flow — we validate the architecture, run validation tests, and create a production variant in our catalog. There can be additional validation time for custom ops.
[02:58] Maya Lopez: Are there constraints on container runtimes, drivers? Our infra includes some proprietary bits and we want to know if that blocks onboarding.
[03:05] Priya Raman: We generally support standard CUDA stacks and some variant of Triton/torchscript. Proprietary bits might need packaging; in Private/on-prem cases we can work with your infra team to integrate drivers. For Dedicated we maintain the runtime and apply kernel patches centrally.
[03:20] Raj Patel: Another operational note: how do you handle autoscaling and burst capacity? Some of our customers run spikey workloads.
[03:28] Darius King: Dedicated has configurable autoscaling and burst options. We can also route to hosted fallbacks during capacity constraints. That's a product-level policy we can set per-customer.
[03:36] Liam O'Connor: Good. On billing, do you prefer to bill end-customer directly or have partner-reseller billing?
[03:42] Avery Chen: Both models supported. Reseller model uses partner invoicing and revenue share, marketplace/managed listing routes revenue to Redwood and credits partners. We'll include this in the partner doc.
[03:52] Tessa Wu: Legal — do you require an MSA? We'd need to route to procurement.
[03:57] Avery Chen: Yes, for reseller/committed Dedicated we do an MSA. We'll give you the draft and the right contact.
[04:04] [00:04:04] Priya Raman: Quick check — any specific benchmarks you want run? Latency p99, throughput for 8k context, memory footprints?
[04:12] Raj Patel: p99 latency for a 4k-8k context generation with an LLM around 70B, and also throughput for RAG workloads (embedding + generation).
[04:21] Priya Raman: OK we'll include configs for 32/64 batch sizes, sequence lengths, and memory usage. We'll also note quant profiles to test.
[04:29] Liam O'Connor: On integration, ideally we'd have an SSO flow so customers using Nimbus console can provision Redwood instances without separate auth. Any SSO/SAML APIs?
[04:37] Darius King: We support SAML/SSO and have some hooks for provisioning via API. For Private deployments there's a deeper integration path.
[04:44] Maya Lopez: How do you handle data residency and logs? Some EU customers need logs retained in-region.
[04:50] Avery Chen: We support region pinning and data residency options on Private/Dedicated; hosted may have region constraints but region pinning is available for enterprise.
[04:58] Tessa Wu: Great. Can Redwood provide an initial security pack and SOC2 report?
[05:03] Darius King: We'll share the security pack and SOC2 artifacts (some redactions possible). We'll need a signed NDA for certain docs if you want the full set.
[05:12] Priya Raman: On the technical POC — we typically do a 2-4 week pilot. Steps: define workload, share dataset (anonymized), pick target metrics, run baseline on your infra, then run Redwood's harness and compare. We can also co-brand a joint case study if successful.
[05:27] Liam O'Connor: That sounds good. Internally we'll need to check which accounts are good fits for a pilot. Probably a couple of mid-market customers who need lower latency.
[05:35] [00:05:35] Avery Chen: Recap from our side — Redwood will: 1) send partner one-pager and high-level commercial options (Avery), 2) Priya will share benchmark spreadsheet + recommended test configs, 3) Darius will loop in Partner Ops to discuss marketplace listing process. Nimbus will: 1) propose pilot workload and data set, 2) confirm procurement/legal contact.
[05:54] Raj Patel: One last technical nit — do you have GPU instance SKU names you validate against? We run into name mismatches in customer infra.
[06:02] Priya Raman: We'll share a hardware profile list — includes validated SKUs, required CUDA/driver versions, NVLink topology notes. Some names may be vendor-branded but we map them in our catalog.
[06:12] Tessa Wu: Timeline — what's realistic for the pilot?
[06:16] Avery Chen: If we get the dataset and pilot definition within a week, we can kick off the POC the week of Dec 15 and get initial benchmarks in 2 weeks. So target deliverables mid-Jan.
[06:26] Liam O'Connor: Good. Anything else from Nimbus?
[06:29] Maya Lopez: Just a note — for marketing we want to align on co-marketing assets. If pilot goes well we'll push a joint announcement.
[06:35] Darius King: Great — we'll put co-marketing on the roadmap after technical sign-off.
[06:40] Avery Chen: Ok, thanks all. We'll follow up with the materials and schedule the kickoff.
[06:45] Liam O'Connor: Thanks everyone, appreciate it.
[06:48] End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription with occasional mis-hears (NVLink sometimes transcribed as "envy link" in rough drafts), speaker labels may be slightly off.
